name: org-lsp
description: Org mode support through the org-lsp language server: highlighting, folding, outline, TODO states and the agenda.

org-lsp.server.path.markdownDescription: Path to the `org-lsp` server binary. When empty, the binary bundled with the extension is used, or else `org-lsp` from `PATH`.

org-lsp.conceal.markdownDescription: Hide what Org hides: link brackets and targets (`linkDescriptive`), and emphasis markers with `hideEmphasisMarkers`. It shows on the lines with a cursor.

enumDescriptions: As notifications, in the corner of the window.
In the status bar for a few seconds, as Emacs's echo area shows them.
org-lsp.messages.markdownDescription: How Org's messages show (`Priority of current item set to A`, `Effort is now 1:00`). Errors always show as notifications.

enumDescriptions: In an editor group below the current one.
In an editor group beside the current one.
In a window of its own.
org-lsp.winSplitMode.markdownDescription: Where the agenda and capture buffers open.

enumDescriptions: Emacs's keys: `Ctrl+C Ctrl+T`, `Tab`, `Shift+arrows`, … in Org files, and Org's single letters in the agenda. `Ctrl+C` then waits for a second key in Org files instead of copying (`Ctrl+Insert` still copies).

The Neovim plugin's keys, for VSCodeVim: those VS Code can bind without taking keys from Vim (`Tab`, `Ctrl+Space`, `Ctrl+A`, …) in Normal mode, and the agenda's. docs/vscode/keys.md shows how to add the leader keys to VSCodeVim.
No keys: bind the commands yourself in keybindings.json.
org-lsp.keys.markdownDescription: Which keys the extension binds in Org files, the agenda, the date prompt and capture buffers.

org-lsp.settings.markdownDescription: The server's options, for example `{ "agendaFiles": ["~/org"], "todoKeywords": ["TODO", "NEXT", "|", "DONE"], "logDone": "time" }`. Without `agendaFiles`, the agenda is built from the Org files in the workspace folders. The options and their defaults are listed in [docs/vscode/configuration.md](https://github.com/kristijanhusak/org-lsp/blob/main/docs/vscode/configuration.md).

config_file.markdownDescription: The shared configuration file, whose options this editor's go on top of: `false` for none, or the path of another file (JSON if it ends in `.json`, else TOML). Unset, it is `$ORG_LSP_CONFIG`, else `config.toml` or `config.json` in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/org-lsp` (`~/.config/org-lsp`; `%APPDATA%\org-lsp` on Windows).

org_agenda_files.markdownDescription: Files, directories and glob patterns (`*`, `?`, `**`) the agenda is built from. `~/` is the home directory, and a directory stands for the Org files directly in it. When empty, the agenda is built from the Org files under the workspace folders (hidden directories, `node_modules` and `target` left out), or else from the Org files that are open. (`org-agenda-files`)

org_todo_keywords.markdownDescription: The TODO sequence, written like Org's `#+TODO:` line. `|` separates the states that count as done; without it the last keyword is the only done state. `TODO(t)` gives a keyword a key for fast selection, and `WAIT(w@/!)` makes it log a note (`@`) or the time (`!`) on entering and leaving it. A file's own `#+TODO:` lines take precedence. (`org-todo-keywords`)

org_log_done.markdownDescription: Write `CLOSED:` with the time when an entry is done, and with `note` ask for a note too. A file's `#+STARTUP:` words `logdone`, `lognotedone` and `nologdone` change it there; an entry's `LOGGING` property (inherited) says what its state changes log instead: those words, `logrepeat` and its relatives, and keywords with what they log (`WAIT(@/!)`), or `nil` for nothing. (`org-log-done`)

org_log_repeat.markdownDescription: Record when a repeating entry is done and moves to its next date. `#+STARTUP:` `logrepeat`, `lognoterepeat` and `nologrepeat` change it in a file, and the `LOGGING` property in an entry. (`org-log-repeat`)

org_log_into_drawer.markdownDescription: Put state changes and notes into a drawer: `true` for `LOGBOOK`, or the name of a drawer. `#+STARTUP:` `logdrawer` and `nologdrawer` change it in a file; an entry's `LOG_INTO_DRAWER` property (inherited) says which drawer for it (`t` for `LOGBOOK`, `nil` for none). (`org-log-into-drawer`)

org_tags_column.markdownDescription: Where tags are aligned after a change to a headline. Negative: they end at that column. (`org-tags-column`)

org_use_tag_inheritance.markdownDescription: Which tags entries inherit from their parents and from `#+FILETAGS:`: `true` for all, `false` for none, a list of tags, or a regexp (Emacs syntax) tags must match. Inherited tags count in tag searches and show in the agenda. (`org-use-tag-inheritance`)

org_tags_exclude_from_inheritance.markdownDescription: Tags never inherited, when `org_use_tag_inheritance` is `true` or a regexp. (`org-tags-exclude-from-inheritance`)

org_use_property_inheritance.markdownDescription: Which properties an entry without them takes from its parents, the file's property drawer and `#+PROPERTY:` lines, in property searches (`OWNER="alice"`): `true` for all, `false` for none, a list of names, or a regexp (Emacs syntax). `CATEGORY` and `ARCHIVE` are always inherited. (`org-use-property-inheritance`)

org_global_properties.markdownDescription: Properties every entry inherits, after those of `#+PROPERTY:` lines: chiefly the allowed values of a property, which setting it offers and `S-<right>` and `S-<left>` go through on its line (`{ "Effort_ALL": "0:10 0:30 1:00 2:00" }`; `:ETC` allows others too). (`org-global-properties`)

org_clock_into_drawer.markdownDescription: Where `CLOCK:` lines go: `true` for the drawer of `org_log_into_drawer` (`LOGBOOK` when that is not a name), the name of a drawer, or `false` for the entry itself. (`org-clock-into-drawer`)

org_clock_out_remove_zero_time_clocks.markdownDescription: Clocking out after less than a minute removes the `CLOCK:` line. (`org-clock-out-remove-zero-time-clocks`)

org_clock_out_when_done.markdownDescription: Marking the clocked entry done stops the clock. (`org-clock-out-when-done`)

org_clock_display_default_range.markdownDescription: The span whose clocks `org.clock.display` (`C-c C-x C-d`) adds up. (`org-clock-display-default-range`)

org_clock_idle_time.markdownDescription: After how many minutes without a message from the editor a clock that runs asks what to do with the idle time: keep it, subtract it (and clock out), or cancel the clock. (`org-clock-idle-time`)

org_clock_history_length.markdownDescription: How many entries clocked into the clock history keeps, for `org.clock.in` with a count and `org.clock.in.last`. (`org-clock-history-length`)

org_clock_clocktable_default_properties.markdownDescription: The parameters a new clock table gets on its `#+BEGIN:` line from `org.clock.report` (`C-c C-x C-r`), after `:scope`, as Emacs Lisp reads them (`:maxlevel 3 :link t`). (`org-clock-clocktable-default-properties`)

org_clock_total_time_cell_format.markdownDescription: How a clock table writes its total time and the words before it; `%s` is the text. (`org-clock-total-time-cell-format`)

org_clock_file_time_cell_format.markdownDescription: How a clock table over several files writes the words before a file's time; `%s` is the text. (`org-clock-file-time-cell-format`)

org_clock_in_switch_to_state.markdownDescription: The TODO state an entry is put in when the clock starts on it (`NEXT`), unless it has it already. (`org-clock-in-switch-to-state`)

org_clock_out_switch_to_state.markdownDescription: The TODO state an entry is put in when the clock stops on it. (`org-clock-out-switch-to-state`)

org_lint.markdownDescription: Org's linter checks the documents and reports what it finds as diagnostics: misplaced headings and planning lines, links to nowhere, duplicate names, footnotes without definitions… A checker Org trusts little reports information, the others warnings. (`org-lint`)

org_lint_ignore.markdownDescription: The `org-lint` checkers to leave out, by name, as a diagnostic's code shows it (`"misplaced-heading"`). (`org-lint`)

org_id_link_to_org_use_id.markdownDescription: Whether `org.link.store` (`C-c l`) links to an entry by its ID: `true` makes one when the entry has none, `"create-if-interactive"` only from the command (not for capture's `%a`), `"create-if-interactive-and-no-custom-id"` likewise unless the entry has a `CUSTOM_ID`, `"use-existing"` only when it has one already. Off, the link searches for the headline. (`org-id-link-to-org-use-id`)

org_link_context_for_files.markdownDescription: Links to a place in a file search for it (`file:notes.org::*Heading`); `C-u` turns it around for one link. (`org-link-context-for-files`)

org_id_link_use_context.markdownDescription: ID links to a place below the entry's headline search for it as well (`id:…::name`). (`org-id-link-use-context`)

org_id_link_consider_parent_id.markdownDescription: An ID link may use the ID of a parent entry, with a search for the place. (`org-id-link-consider-parent-id`)

org_link_file_path_type.markdownDescription: How links to files write the path: `"adaptive"` relative below the file's directory and absolute elsewhere, `"absolute"` (with `~`), `"noabbrev"` (without), `"relative"`. (`org-link-file-path-type`)

org_link_keep_stored_after_insertion.markdownDescription: Stored links stay stored once inserted. (`org-link-keep-stored-after-insertion`)

org_complete_tags_always_offer_all_agend.markdownDescription: Completing a tag offers the tags of every agenda file, after those of the file. Off, only the file's own. Setting tags offers them too. (`org-complete-tags-always-offer-all-agenda-tags`)

org_cite_global_bibliography.markdownDescription: Bibliography files for the citations of every document (`[cite:@key]`), after those its `#+BIBLIOGRAPHY:` lines name: BibTeX (`.bib`, `.bibtex`) or CSL-JSON (`.json`). Their entries are completed after `@`, shown over a key, and where following a key goes; a key none has is marked. (`org-cite-global-bibliography`)

org_tag_alist.markdownDescription: The tags offered when setting tags in a file without a `#+TAGS:` line, written like one: `"work(w) home(h) { @office(o) @home(m) } [ GTD : Control Persp ]"` gives `work` the key `w`, makes `@office` and `@home` exclusive, and groups `Control` and `Persp` under `GTD`; `\n` starts a new line. A list of these words does as well. Unset, the tags used in the file are offered. (`org-tag-alist`)

org_tag_persistent_alist.markdownDescription: Tags offered in every file, before those of `#+TAGS:` or `org_tag_alist`, written the same way. (`org-tag-persistent-alist`)

org_group_tags.markdownDescription: A group tag (`[ GTD : Control Persp ]`, `{ Context : @home @office }` in `#+TAGS:` or `org_tag_alist`) in the match string of a tags view stands for itself and the tags of its group. (`org-group-tags`)

org_use_fast_tag_selection.markdownDescription: Pick tags by key, each key turning its tag on or off until RET: `auto` when some tag has a key, `true` always (keys are given to the tags without one), `false` never: the tags are typed instead. (`org-use-fast-tag-selection`)

org_fast_tag_selection_single_key.markdownDescription: In fast tag selection, the first key that changes the tags also ends it. (`org-fast-tag-selection-single-key`)

org_tags_sort_function.markdownDescription: Sort the tags of a headline when they are set: alphabetically, or the other way. (`org-tags-sort-function`)

org_auto_align_tags.markdownDescription: Align the tags of a headline to `org_tags_column` when they are set. (`org-auto-align-tags`)

org_todo_repeat_to_state.markdownDescription: The state a repeating entry returns to when it is done: a keyword, or `true` for the state it had. (`org-todo-repeat-to-state`)

org_priority_default.markdownDescription: The priority of an entry without a cookie. A file's `#+PRIORITIES:` line takes precedence over the three priority options. (`org-priority-default`)

org_priority_start_cycle_with_default.markdownDescription: Raising or lowering the priority of an entry that has none starts at the default. (`org-priority-start-cycle-with-default`)

org_time_stamp_rounding_minutes.markdownDescription: The step in which the minutes of a timestamp change (the second number of Org's option). (`org-time-stamp-rounding-minutes`)

org_read_date_prefer_future.markdownDescription: A date typed without a year or month is the next one to come. With `time`, a time that has passed today is tomorrow's. (`org-read-date-prefer-future`)

org_read_date_force_compatible_dates.markdownDescription: A typed year is kept within 1970 to 2037. (`org-read-date-force-compatible-dates`)

files.description: `current` (the entry's own file), `agenda`, a path or a list of paths

maxlevel.description: The headlines up to this level

regexp.description: The headlines that match this regular expression

todo.description: The headlines with this TODO keyword

org_refile_targets.markdownDescription: Where entries can be refiled to. Each entry has `files`: `current` (the entry's own file), `agenda`, a path or a list of paths; and one of `level`, `maxlevel`, `tag`, `todo`, `regexp` (the Rust `regex` crate's syntax) or `all` (true), which says which headlines there are targets. (`org-refile-targets`)

org_refile_use_outline_path.markdownDescription: Name targets by their outline path (`Projects/Alpha/`). The three names start the path with the file, and offer the file itself, for its top level. (`org-refile-use-outline-path`)

org_reverse_note_order.markdownDescription: A refiled entry goes first under its target, not last. (`org-reverse-note-order`)

org_archive_location.markdownDescription: Where archived subtrees go: a file, `::`, and a headline under which they go (they go to the end of the file without one). `%s` is the name of the file the subtree is in; an empty file part is that file. `datetree/` as the headline files them under year, month and day, by when they were closed. An `ARCHIVE` property of the entry or a parent, or a `#+ARCHIVE:` line, says otherwise. (`org-archive-location`)

org_archive_reversed_order.markdownDescription: An archived subtree goes first under its archive headline, not last. (`org-archive-reversed-order`)

org_archive_mark_done.markdownDescription: Mark archived entries done: `true` for the first done keyword, or the keyword to use. (`org-archive-mark-done`)

org_archive_subtree_add_inherited_tags.markdownDescription: Give an archived subtree the tags it inherited: always, never, or when it stays in its file. (`org-archive-subtree-add-inherited-tags`)

org_archive_save_context_info.markdownDescription: What an archived entry keeps as `ARCHIVE_…` properties: `time`, `file`, `olpath` (its outline path), `category`, `todo`, `itags` (inherited tags), `ltags` (its own tags) and `olid` (its parent's ID). (`org-archive-save-context-info`)

org_archive_sibling_heading.markdownDescription: The headline of the sibling `org.archive.sibling` archives under. (`org-archive-sibling-heading`)

org_archive_file_header_format.markdownDescription: What a new archive file starts with; `%s` is the path of the file the subtree came from. (`org-archive-file-header-format`)

org_archive_default_command.markdownDescription: What `org.archive.default` does: archive the subtree, archive it under its sibling, or tag it. (`org-archive-default-command`)

clock_in.description: Clock the captured entry while the capture goes on

clock_keep.description: Keep the clock running when the capture is filed

clock_resume.description: Start the clock the capture stopped again

jump_to_captured.description: Show the captured entry in its file

key.description: The keys that pick the template

prepend.description: First under the target, not last

table_line_pos.description: Where a table line goes: `II-1` is above the second rule

target.description: `file` and a path; `file+headline`, a path and a headline; `file+olp`, a path and the headlines of an outline path; `file+regexp`, a path and a regular expression; `file+olp+datetree`, a path and maybe an outline path; `id` and an ID; or `clock`

time_prompt.description: Ask for the date of the date tree entry

tree_type.description: The levels of a date tree

type.description: An Org entry (the default), plain text, a list item, a checkbox item or a table line

org_capture_templates.markdownDescription: Capture templates. Each has a `key`, a `description`, a `type` (`entry`, the default, `plain`, `item`, `checkitem` or `table-line`), a `target` and a `template` (text, or a list of lines), and may have `prepend`, `empty_lines`, `empty_lines_before`, `empty_lines_after`, `immediate_finish`, `tree_type`, `time_prompt`, `table_line_pos`, `clock_in`, `clock_keep`, `clock_resume` and `jump_to_captured`. The target is a list: `file` and a path; `file+headline`, a path and a headline; `file+olp`, a path and the headlines of an outline path; `file+regexp`, a path and a regular expression; `file+olp+datetree`, a path and the headlines of an outline path, maybe none, for a date tree under them; `id` and an ID; or `clock`, the entry clocked now. An empty path is `org_default_notes_file`, and without a target the entry goes at the end of `org_default_notes_file`. A template with only a key and a description groups the templates whose keys start with its key. (`org-capture-templates`)

org_directory.markdownDescription: Where the relative paths of capture targets are. (`org-directory`)

org_default_notes_file.markdownDescription: The target of a capture template whose file is empty. (`org-default-notes-file`)

org_link_descriptive.markdownDescription: Show a link as its description (or its target, when it has none) and hide the rest: the brackets, and the target of a link with a description. The text is marked `hidden` in the highlighting, and editors that can conceal text conceal it. (`org-link-descriptive`)

org_hide_emphasis_markers.markdownDescription: Hide the markers around `*bold*`, `/italic/`, `_underline_`, `+strike-through+`, `=verbatim=` and `~code~`, as for links. (`org-hide-emphasis-markers`)

return_uses_meta_return.markdownDescription: RET on the first line of a list item makes the next item, numbered and with a checkbox as M-RET (`org-meta-return`) makes it, the items after it renumbered, as nvim-orgmode's `org_return_uses_meta_return` does. Off, RET is Org's: a new line in the item. `org.return.item` (`<S-CR>`, Shift+Enter, with the vim keys) always does it.

calendar_months.markdownDescription: How many months the calendar of the date prompt shows: 3 side by side, as Emacs's calendar shows them, the one with the selected day in the middle; or 1, that month alone, for a narrow window.

emacs.markdownDescription: The Emacs program, for what only Org itself does: export (`org.export.dispatch`). The server starts it (`emacs --batch -Q`) when that is first asked for and keeps it running, so that Org loads once. Without Emacs, everything else works as before.

emacs_config_file.markdownDescription: A file of Emacs Lisp that Emacs loads before Org, for the variables export reads (`org-export-backends`, `org-html-…`, `org-latex-…`, `org-publish-project-alist`): a file of its own, or your init file. `~/` is the home directory.

emacs_config.markdownDescription: Emacs Lisp that Emacs evaluates after `emacs_config_file` and before loading Org, for a few settings without a file: `(setq org-export-with-toc nil)`, or `(add-to-list 'load-path "~/src/org-mode/lisp")` for another Org. A yes-or-no question Emacs asks while it works (`org-confirm-babel-evaluate`) is asked in the editor.

auto_save.markdownDescription: Save the files a command changes other than the one it was run in: an entry's file changed from the agenda, the target of a capture or of a refile. The editor saves them once it has made the change. Off, they are left with unsaved changes, as Emacs leaves them.

org_cycle_separator_lines.markdownDescription: With at least this many blank lines after a subtree, the last one stays outside its fold. Negative: all of them stay outside. `0`: none does. (`org-cycle-separator-lines`)

org_adapt_indentation.markdownDescription: Indent the lines of an entry past its headline's stars: `true` for all of them, `"headline-data"` for the planning line, drawers and clock lines right below the headline. Applies to new lines, to re-indenting (range formatting) and to what commands write. (`org-adapt-indentation`)

org_startup_indented.markdownDescription: Show files indented by level without changing them (`org-indent-mode`): the text under a headline lines up with its title, and leading stars are hidden. `#+STARTUP: indent` and `noindent` decide for a file. It turns `org_adapt_indentation` off in such files, unless that is `"headline-data"`. Editors that can show it: Neovim, and VS Code (not on wrapped lines). (`org-startup-indented`)

org_hide_leading_stars.markdownDescription: Hide all the stars of a headline but the last; they keep their place. `#+STARTUP: hidestars` and `showstars` decide for a file. (`org-hide-leading-stars`)

org_src_preserve_indentation.markdownDescription: Leave the code of source blocks as it is indented when re-indenting. (`org-src-preserve-indentation`)

org_edit_src_content_indentation.markdownDescription: How far code is indented past its source block when re-indenting. (`org-edit-src-content-indentation`)

org_agenda_span.markdownDescription: How much time the agenda shows. (`org-agenda-span`)

org_agenda_start_on_weekday.markdownDescription: The day a week or fortnight starts on; `false` starts it today. (`org-agenda-start-on-weekday`)

org_deadline_warning_days.markdownDescription: How many days before a deadline it shows up. (`org-deadline-warning-days`)

org_scheduled_delay_days.markdownDescription: How many days after its date a scheduled entry shows up. (`org-scheduled-delay-days`)

org_scheduled_past_days.markdownDescription: How many days a scheduled entry that is not done keeps showing up. (`org-scheduled-past-days`)

org_deadline_past_days.markdownDescription: How many days a missed deadline keeps showing up. (`org-deadline-past-days`)

org_agenda_skip_scheduled_if_done.markdownDescription: Leave out scheduled entries that are done. (`org-agenda-skip-scheduled-if-done`)

org_agenda_skip_deadline_if_done.markdownDescription: Leave out deadlines of entries that are done. (`org-agenda-skip-deadline-if-done`)

org_agenda_skip_timestamp_if_done.markdownDescription: Leave out timestamps of entries that are done. (`org-agenda-skip-timestamp-if-done`)

org_agenda_show_future_repeats.markdownDescription: Show the future dates of repeating entries: all of them, none, or only the next. (`org-agenda-show-future-repeats`)

org_agenda_tags_column.markdownDescription: Where tags are aligned in the agenda: a column (negative: where they end), or `auto` for the right edge of the window. With `auto`, the editors that tell the server how wide the agenda's window is (Neovim, Vim, Sublime Text) have the tags there, and the agenda follows the window as it is resized; the others (VS Code, Zed) have them end at column 80. (`org-agenda-tags-column`)

org_agenda_time_grid.markdownDescription: The time grid, as Org writes it: the days that have it (`daily`: a one-day agenda; `weekly`: every day of a longer one; `today`: today; `require-timed`: only days with an entry that has a time; `remove-match`: no grid line at a time an entry already has), the times of its lines (`800` for 8:00), what follows a time that has no end time, and the text of a grid line. (`org-agenda-time-grid`)

org_agenda_current_time_string.markdownDescription: The text of the line for the current time. (`org-agenda-current-time-string`)

org_agenda_show_current_time_in_grid.markdownDescription: Show the current time in the grid. (`org-agenda-show-current-time-in-grid`)

org_agenda_weekend_days.markdownDescription: The days drawn as the weekend (0 is Sunday). (`org-agenda-weekend-days`)

org_agenda_start_with_log_mode.markdownDescription: Start the agenda in log mode, which shows what was closed and clocked each day (`l` toggles it). (`org-agenda-start-with-log-mode`)

org_agenda_start_with_clockreport_mode.markdownDescription: Start the agenda with the clock report under it (`R` toggles it). (`org-agenda-start-with-clockreport-mode`)

org_agenda_start_with_archives_mode.markdownDescription: Start the agenda with entries in archived trees (`trees`; `v a` toggles it), or those and the files the agenda files archive to (`files`; `v A`). (`org-agenda-start-with-archives-mode`)

org_agenda_log_mode_items.markdownDescription: What log mode shows: `closed` entries, `clock` lines and `state` changes. (`org-agenda-log-mode-items`)

org_agenda_persistent_marks.markdownDescription: Keep the marks of a bulk action (`B`) after it (`p` in its menu toggles this for one action). (`org-agenda-persistent-marks`)

org_agenda_start_with_follow_mode.markdownDescription: Start the agenda in follow mode, which shows the entry of the cursor's line in another window as the cursor moves (`F` toggles it). (`org-agenda-start-with-follow-mode`)

org_agenda_start_with_entry_text_mode.markdownDescription: Start the agenda with some text of each entry under its line (`E` toggles it). (`org-agenda-start-with-entry-text-mode`)

org_agenda_entry_text_maxlines.markdownDescription: The most lines of an entry's text `E` shows. (`org-agenda-entry-text-maxlines`)

org_agenda_entry_text_leaders.markdownDescription: What each line of an entry's text starts with in the agenda. (`org-agenda-entry-text-leaders`)

org_agenda_entry_text_exclude_regexps.markdownDescription: Emacs regexps whose matches are left out of the entry text `E` shows. (`org-agenda-entry-text-exclude-regexps`)

org_agenda_block_separator.markdownDescription: What goes between the blocks of a block agenda: one character repeated across 79 columns, a longer text as it is, or `false` for nothing. In a block's `settings`, the separator above that block. (`org-agenda-block-separator`)

org_agenda_compact_blocks.markdownDescription: Leave out the separators between blocks and the header over agenda blocks. (`org-agenda-compact-blocks`)

agenda_hide_empty_blocks.markdownDescription: Leave out the blocks of a block agenda that show no entries. Not in Org.

org_agenda_search_view_always_boolean.markdownDescription: Read every search string of the search view (`s`) as words that must (`+word`, `word`) or must not (`-word`) occur, `{regexp}`s and `"quoted phrases"`. Off, it is a phrase whose spaces match any whitespace, unless its first word starts with `+`, `-` or `{`. (`org-agenda-search-view-always-boolean`)

org_agenda_search_view_force_full_words.markdownDescription: The words of a Boolean search match whole words only, as a search string starting with `:` asks. (`org-agenda-search-view-force-full-words`)

org_agenda_search_view_max_outline_level.markdownDescription: The search view shows headlines down to this level, a match below one counting for the headline above: 0 for every level. (`org-agenda-search-view-max-outline-level`)

org_agenda_text_search_extra_files.markdownDescription: Files the search view (`s`) searches besides the agenda files, after them, as `org_agenda_files` names them. `agenda-archives` first adds the files the agenda files archive to. A file listed twice is searched at its last place. (`org-agenda-text-search-extra-files`)

org_agenda_prefix_format.markdownDescription: What comes before the headline on a line of the agenda (`agenda`), the TODO list (`todo`), tags searches (`tags`) and text searches (`search`): `%c` the category, `%t` the time, `%s` the leader (`Scheduled: `), `%e` the effort, `%l` a blank per level, `%T` the last tag, `%b` the headlines above (breadcrumbs), `%i` the icon (none). A width pads (`%-12c` on the right, `%12c` on the left), `.N` cuts, `%?` leaves out an empty field, and a character before the letter follows a value that is not empty (`%-12:c`). `%(…)` (Emacs Lisp) is left empty. (`org-agenda-prefix-format`)

org_agenda_todo_keyword_format.markdownDescription: How a TODO keyword is written in the agenda: `%-4s` pads it to four columns, so that the titles line up; an empty format leaves keywords out. (`org-agenda-todo-keyword-format`)

org_agenda_scheduled_leaders.markdownDescription: The leader of a scheduled entry on its day, and on today when its day has passed (`%d`: the days since). (`org-agenda-scheduled-leaders`)

org_agenda_deadline_leaders.markdownDescription: The leader of a deadline on its day, on today before it (`%d`: the days left), and on today after it (`%d`: the days since). (`org-agenda-deadline-leaders`)

org_agenda_timerange_leaders.markdownDescription: The leader of a time range within a day, and of a range over days (`%d`: which day of it, `%d`: how many days). (`org-agenda-timerange-leaders`)

org_agenda_remove_tags.markdownDescription: Leave the tags out of the agenda's lines; `prefix` only when the prefix shows a tag (`%T`). (`org-agenda-remove-tags`)

org_stuck_projects.markdownDescription: What the stuck projects view (`#`) lists: the projects the match string finds whose subtree has no entry with one of the TODO keywords (`*` for any not done) or tags (`*` for any), and no match of the regexp. (`org-stuck-projects`)

org_agenda_breadcrumbs_separator.markdownDescription: What goes between the headlines of `%b`. (`org-agenda-breadcrumbs-separator`)

org_agenda_format_date.markdownDescription: How the agenda writes a day, as `format-time-string` does: `%A %d %B %Y`, `%a %Y-%m-%d`. (`org-agenda-format-date`)

org_agenda_start_day.markdownDescription: The day the agenda starts from, as the date prompt reads it: `-1d`, `+2d`, `2026-10-01`. (`org-agenda-start-day`)

blocks.description: Views shown one after the other

header.description: Replaces the view's header; empty for none

match.description: For todo, keywords; for tags, a match string

settings.description: Agenda options for this block: org_agenda_span, org_agenda_start_day…

header.description: Replaces the view's header; empty for none

key.description: The keys that pick the command in the agenda menu

match.description: For todo, keywords (NEXT|WAIT); for tags, a match string (work-home, PRIORITY="A")

settings.description: Agenda options for this command: org_agenda_span, org_agenda_start_day…

org_agenda_custom_commands.markdownDescription: Commands of the agenda menu. Each has a `key` and a `description`, and either a `type` (`agenda`, `alltodo`, `todo`, `tags` or `tags-todo`) with a `match` (keywords such as `NEXT|WAIT` for `todo`, a match string such as `work-home` or `PRIORITY="A"` for `tags`), or `blocks`, a list of such views shown one after the other. `header` replaces a view's header (empty: none), and `settings` holds agenda options for the command or a block (`org_agenda_span`, `org_agenda_start_day`…). A command with only a key and a description groups the commands whose keys start with its key. (`org-agenda-custom-commands`)
